Hi Olivia — thanks, and great questions. Below is a concise mapping and the controls available. I'm attaching a one-page data matrix for BetaSMC's review (redwood-data-matrix-20290618.pdf).

Summary (hosted API default behavior):
- Raw prompts: not persisted for model training; short-term request traces used for debugging are retained for 24 hours and then purged by default.
- Model outputs / derivatives: we retain generated outputs for 30 days by default for quality monitoring and safety reviews. This includes text responses and any derived embeddings.
- Request/response logs & KV cache: full debug logs are available but not retained beyond the configured TTL; support access is role-based and gated (see notes below).
- Data residency: hosted customers can select region (US/EU) at signup; for strict US-only residency we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private (VPC) where you control physical region and retention policies.

Controls & enterprise options:
- TTL override: For Dedicated and Private deployments we can set TTL=0 (no persisted copies) for prompts and/or outputs as a contractual setting.
- Logging opt-out: Request/response storing and debug-level traces can be disabled at the tenant level; support access requires a documented request with RBAC approval.
- Access & audit: Audit logs for who requested data are retained and included in the enterprise audit package.

Evidence & next steps (what I can share right away):
- Redwood SOC2 summary (we'll provide the summary PDF and redacted report).
- Data matrix (attached) that maps exactly what fields are persisted and where.
- Draft DPA clause language we can drop into your order form.

Action items: 
1) I attached redwood-data-matrix-20290618.pdf — please confirm it covers your questions.
2) Monica will pull the SOC2 summary and DPA draft and loop them into this thread by tomorrow morning.
3) If BetaSMC needs TTL=0 and US-only residency we should scope Dedicated/Private in the order form (Ben — can you prepare a rough cost delta to include in the SOW?).

Rajiv / Olivia — thanks, answers below and attaching the artifacts you requested. Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary-202806.pdf, redwood-data-matrix-20290618.pdf, dpa-draft-betasmc.docx

Direct answers:
- "Derivatives": Yes — embeddings, vectors, and any token-level metadata are treated the same as textual outputs in our retention model. The data matrix (attached) shows which artifact classes map to which TTL and storage region.
- TTL=0: Hosted (multi-tenant) customers default to 30 days and do not have a self-serve TTL=0 option. TTL=0 (no persistent storage of user inputs or derivatives) is available as a contractual setting on Redwood Dedicated or Private deployments. We'll include firm language in the DPA draft to reflect that.
- Support access: Support and Engineering do NOT have automatic read access to customer prompts/derivatives. Access requires an internal request reviewed by the security team and is logged in an audit trail. We can add a clause in the DPA that any access to content requires explicit written approval from BetaSMC's security contact.

Suggested procurement-ready text (drop-in):
"Redwood will not persist customer-provided prompts or generated derivatives beyond the mutually agreed TTL. For Dedicated or Private deployments, the TTL may be set to 0, meaning no persisted copies of prompts or derivatives will be retained by Redwood. Access to any persisted data by Redwood employees requires documented approval from the customer's designated security contact and will be recorded in audit logs."
